Hi, I am working on perfect graphs. An intermediate result requires me to prove that if two graphs are isomorphic, their clique number and chromatic number is same.
I wanted to know if there is support in Lean 4 to prove that any general property which can be expressed in second order monadic logic for graphs will be true for G1 iff it's true for G2 where G1 and G2 are isomporhic.
If there is no support, how would one go about building such a system?

Chintada Srinivasa said:

I wanted to know if there is support in Lean 4 to prove that any general property which can be expressed in second order monadic logic for graphs will be true for G1 iff it's true for G2 where G1 and G2 are isomporhic.

I believe there isn't, but also I suggest separating this cool theorem from the issue at hand.
It's probably much easier to prove isomorphism theorems for clique/chromatic numbers than proving this theorem, and presumably this general statement will depend on a lot of model theory and Mathlib prefers not importing what you don't have to.

btw I'm very surprised we don't have these, you're welcome to PR! I might also try to help

Do you have any resources on where I can learn about Modelling inductive types and logic in Lean and how lean handles logic. I was thinking if it could be defined inductively, then given a definition, it would attempt to break it down inductively to get a proof of being second order logic. Something like

def IsMonadicSecondOrder (d : function) : Prop :=
-- variables (v, e, X (vertex set), C (edge set))
-- atomics (v : V, inc(e, v), x = y)
-- Boolean formulae (¬, ∧, ∨, →)
-- Quantifiers (∀, ∃)

Coincidentally, I think reading this thread #Type theory > translation of constructive proofs written in lean @ 💬 would help, as I assume you're not familiar with modeling logic/programming-languages in a theorem prover. You could also read Software Foundations Vol 1 if you don't mind switching to Rocq for a brief period.
